description (blank line = new paragraph):
What do a rhino’s horn, a parrot’s beak, a porcupine’s quills, a whale’s giant mouth-comb, and your own fingernails have in common? They are all built from the same stuff: keratin. It is light, tough, bendy, and keeps growing back. Animals have turned it into armor, weapons, raincoats, and wings, but not every animal is in the club.

Bring paper and a pencil. We’ll sort the members from the imposters, work out how many meters of hair your head grows in a day, and argue about why nature picked one material for so many jobs.

Sometimes we get lucky in life, but more often than not, our results reflect the preparation we put in at the start. From basic project planning to de-risking strategies and advanced contingency planning, we can help our ideas “meet with a success unexpected in common hours,” to quote Thoreau.

Join us as we talk about how to help our ideas reach the summit of their potential, working through a plan for your project or idea as we go.

Fourfold, a game developed by Jo, is back for challenge week with new topics, creating a fun and educational environment for practicing teamwork. Remember that nobody can beat Fourfold without working with others, so be prepared to coordinate and collaborate, and work on what effective communication looks like in a fast-paced, time-limited environment!

topic: The Traffic Problem Nobody Can Solve
description (blank line = new paragraph): Join in as we look at real-world problem solving that will test your creativity and ability to leverage tools such as optimization, second-order effects, and consideration of local and collective benefits.
Calling all of our cadet writers! We’ll be exploring how to use dialogue and other tools to make our characters come alive on the page and in the hearts of our audience.

For every planned speech you give throughout your life, you’ll give countless more unplanned with mere seconds of notice, often with high stakes riding on your ability to spontaneously convey and convince. We’ll practice impromptu public speaking in a variety of formats from the quasi-impromptu of the elevator speech to the truly impromptu of answering questions with no advance knowledge of the topic.

For cadets who dread being put on the spot, this is the perfect time to practice these skills in a safe, supportive environment, and for those who love public speaking, we’ll have a lot of fun putting your skills to the test!

Your team will race to clear a Mahjong-style board by matching tiles that mean the same thing, from fractions and percentages to the periodic table. The catch? Each of you can see only part of the board, so you’ll have to talk your way to the top of the leaderboard!

This topic had such challenge potential that we held off doing it last week in order to turn it into a full challenge this week!

The cadets will be doing a deep dive into behavioral and organizational psychology, using the parameters of three different future space missions as their sandbox. They will decide what characteristics are important, and essentially, how they would test and screen for those characteristics in their applicant pool, before seeing whether their mission is a success or failure based upon their choices.

Each team will present their findings to a review board, and defend the thinking behind their approach, giving them practice with their presentation and oratory skills.

We have a guest host this week who is coming to demonstrate powerful tricks to help you memorize everything from spelling to history facts and more, even if you typically think of yourself as someone who has trouble with spelling and other tasks that require memorization.

Can you design a house without any straight lines? Bring paper and pencils, plus anything round and/or squishy you can experiment with (e.g., playdough, clay, foil, a bowl). If you want to use Minecraft or Blender, have them open. No corners are allowed, but someone has to be able to live in the structure!

It’s challenge week, which means cadets will be working in teams to practice communication and collaboration skills while learning along the way!

This week’s focus is economic consolidation, and the ever-evolving ownership behind even legacy brands. The cadets will be challenged to learn about the web of ownership, trace familiar brands back to their institutional owners, and discuss / debate the very real costs and benefits of such consolidation on industry efficiency, consumers, suppliers, vendors, retailers, etc.

This is a great on-ramp to a wide variety of economic and financial topics, so a challenge not to be missed!

We’ll explore why words that sound so similar really are not similar at all, including which one is in nuclear power stations, how sci-fi the other is, and what iron has to do with it all. Join us in this far-flung adventure that reaches all the way to the stars!

In a world filled to the brim with opinions and arguments, understanding which are solid and which are suspicious becomes its own superpower. We’ll look at common logical fallacies, what they sound and look like in use, and how to fight back with critical thinking and questioning.

Sunil Singh, an author, speaker, and passionate educator, joined us as a special guest to regale the students with math as it can, and arguably should, be explored: in ways that spark creativity and make the subject come alive in curious minds.

Mr. Singh believes in the power of mathematical stories and views mathematics as a needed interdisciplinary subject for the future. To help students see the power and potential of math, he seeks to return the subject to the Renaissance era of artistic and philosophical wonder.

He has spoken around the world, including at New York’s Museum of Mathematics and Toronto’s Fields Institute, and in 2021, the United States Commission on Mathematics Instruction invited him to present a webinar on culturally responsive mathematics.

He also runs his own online mathematics school. To learn more, visit https://mathsings.com.

topic: Cogito Ergo Sum: The Logic of Being
description (blank line = new paragraph): We’re going to dive into philosophy this week to look at the arguments surrounding existence, from Augustine and Descartes to modern variations, all attempting to answer the same foundational question: do we know that we exist? Come prepared to discuss, debate, and challenge your own reasoning!

The cadets will be dividing up into teams this week to work on a challenge ripped straight from the headlines: AI policy.

Each team will work to develop a proposed approach to AI development, analyze the impacts of their proposal using the Seventh Generation framework, and then take turns red teaming the proposals of the other groups.

Do not worry if your child doesn’t know much or anything about AI, as we will have groups designed for all knowledge levels!

A riddle within a maze composed of riddles... How soon can you find the ultimate answer? Join in the fun as we play with language’s most artistic format, and seek the answers that unlock the riddles that complicate your path!

Join us as we explore systems thinking with the help of what might seem like an unlikely challenge: growing an alien plant. Systems thinking is the art and science of understanding the pieces that influence complexity, and knowing how to leverage that understanding into a superior familiarity with individual systems and the systems with which they interact.

Buckle up, because we are going to be whizzing back and forth in time in an effort to better understand the scale of history, particularly the eras that eclipse the existence of human civilizations. You’ll walk away with a fresh perspective, an amazing tool for explaining the scope of history to others, and a growing familiarity and comfort with the vocabulary that helps us talk about time and history as more than dates, places, and names.
